# Results — Study 351 (BTC 5-minute Polymarket momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The viral "$300 → $14,000"
Polymarket bot, tested on a real Bitcoin tape. Polymarket's **BTC Up/Down 5-minute** market
resolves **Up** iff the close price ≥ the open price of the 5-minute window (Chainlink BTC/USD
feed). We fold real 1-minute BTC bars into those windows and measure the strategy's two halves:
the continuation win-rate **w** (the signal) and the price **p** you actually pay (the live
CLOB ask). Offline, deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | Binance BTCUSDT 1-minute klines (public endpoint, no key) |
| Window | 2026-05-06 → 2026-06-20 (45 days; 64,801 1m bars → **12,959** 5-minute windows) |
| Resolution model | Up iff close ≥ open of the 5-minute window (Polymarket/Chainlink rule) |
| Live prices | Polymarket CLOB best ask (`clob.polymarket.com`), read-only capture 2026-06-20 |
| BTC range | $59,207 – $82,761 · P(up) = 0.4949 · median \|2-min-left move\| = $32 (90th pct $109) |

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* — one 45-day regime; the continuation
> *probability* is robust (huge z), the exact win-rate is regime-conditioned. *Tradability* —
> the live capture is 32 windows; the **all-bucket** edge is decisive, but the $70-signal
> sub-sample (n=4) is far too small to pin the *sign* of a ~3% edge (≈400–500 signal windows
> needed). The mirage verdict rests on the structural identity p ≈ w plus the spread, not on
> the underpowered signal sub-sample.

## Half 1 — the signal is REAL (continuation win-rate, 2 minutes left)

Among windows that have already moved ≥ $D at the 2-minute mark, how often does the close
finish on the move's side? Binomial *z* is against a coin (0.5).

| head-start D | n (signals) | % of windows | win-rate w | binomial z |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $30 | 6,802 | 52.5% | 89.1% | 64.5 |
| $50 | 4,322 | 33.4% | 92.9% | 56.5 |
| **$70** | **2,759** | **21.3%** | **94.8%** | **47.0** |
| $85 | 2,017 | 15.6% | 96.3% | 41.6 |
| $100 | 1,533 | 11.8% | 96.5% | 36.4 |
| $150 | 620 | 4.8% | 98.6% | 24.2 |

At **1 minute left** it is sharper still: $70 → **98.2%** (n=3,324, z=55.6), $100 → 99.3%.
Momentum into the close is a genuine, monotone, overwhelmingly significant effect.

## Half 2 — the edge is a MIRAGE (price ≈ win-rate)

EV per share of a binary bought at price *p* that wins with prob *w* is exactly **w − p**.
The live Polymarket ask of the favoured side sits on top of its own win-rate:

| live bucket | n | realised w | avg ask p | edge w − p | EV per $ staked |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| all captured windows | 32 | 65.6% | $0.764 | **−0.108** | −0.156 |
| signal (move ≥ $70) | 4 | — | $0.97 | *(underpowered — n too small)* | — |
| strong (move ≥ $100) | 1 | — | $0.99 | *(n=1)* | — |

Representative live tick: BTC moved **−$30** with ~70s left → favoured side (*Down*) quoted
**$0.97**, loser (*Up*) **$0.04**. The favourite is **never** the advertised $0.80 when the
move is real — a cheap ask exists only where the outcome is genuinely uncertain (so w is low
too). Buying the favourite lost money on average across the capture. The bot's own YAML
tolerates a **3¢** spread and a **$30** top-of-book — both adverse, both larger than any gross
edge.

## Half 3 — "$300 → $14,000" is a martingale survivor

Monte-Carlo, 200,000 paths, start $300, target $14,000, win-rate w = 94.8% (D=$70):

| scenario | buy price p | edge (w−p) | P(reach $14k) | P(ruin <$1) | median end |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **fair price, bet 50%/round** | 0.948 | −0.000 | **1.07%** | **39.7%** | $4 |
| pay +5¢ over fair, bet 50% | 0.990 | −0.042 | 0.00% | 99.3% | $0 |
| buy 0.85 (*if* it existed), bet 50% | 0.850 | +0.098 | 100.0% | 0.0% | $14,668 |
| buy 0.85, bet 5% (YAML sizing) | 0.850 | +0.098 | 0.00% | 0.0% | $2,853 |

Even on a **fair coin** (zero house edge), 50%-of-stack sizing ruins ~40% of players and lands
only ~1% at $14,000. The viral post is that 1%. The only row that reaches the jackpot reliably
assumes a $0.80–0.85 favourite that the live book never offers on a decided market.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic arithmetic-Brownian tape with known per-minute σ, the measured continuation
equals the closed-form conditional expectation E[Φ(|move|/σ√2) | |move| ≥ 70], and pricing at
the fair p = w zeroes the EV exactly:

| σ per minute | measured w | exact E[Φ] | fair-price EV (p=w) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| $30 | 98.0% | 98.0% | +0.0000 |
| $45 | 94.2% | 94.3% | +0.0000 |
| $60 | 91.3% | 91.3% | +0.0000 |

Higher σ → lower w *and* a lower fair price in lock-step: there is no volatility at which the
favourite is a bargain.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Continuation at a $70 / 2-min-left head-start is 94.8% (binomial z = 47.0,
  n = 2,759), monotone in the threshold, sharper at 1-minute-left. Momentum into the close is a
  genuine, large-z effect on the real tape — no asterisk.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** EV = w − p, and the live favoured ask is $0.95–0.99 ≈ w. Gross edge
  ~0, negative after the 3¢ spread and thin ($30) book the bot itself flags. The price is
  endogenous to the signal; the cheap quote the pitch promises does not exist when the move is
  real.
- **Get rich quick? — BUSTED.** At fair pricing and 50%/round, P($300→$14k) = 1.1%, P(ruin) =
  40%; pay 5¢ over fair and ruin is ~99%. The viral result is a heavy-tailed bet's lucky
  survivor, the same high-win-rate / negative-expectancy martingale signature as Study 301.

> **Security note (not a results claim, but the real risk).** The advertised repo ships only a
> wrapper; the order engine that signs trades and reads the wallet **private key** lives in a
> separate, unpublished repo. Running it means handing an unaudited program your keys — a larger
> hazard than the negative EV.
